summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived entry on the 1937 Disney animated feature Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. It covers the film's premiere and nationwide release dates, its commercial success including early international earnings, its repeated theatrical re-releases before the 1990s home video release, and its inflation-adjusted standing at the North American box office. It also includes a brief character description of Snow White as voiced by Adriana Caselotti.
one_line: Overview of the 1937 animated film Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, its release history, box office success, and lead character.
key_facts: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premiered at the Carthay Circle Theatre on December 21, 1937.
The film had a nationwide release on February 4, 1938.
The film was a critical and commercial success.
During its initial release, the film earned $8 million in international earnings.
With those international earnings, the film briefly assumed the record of highest-grossing sound film at the time.
The film was re-released theatrically many times, until its home video release in the 1990s.
Adjusted for inflation, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs is one of the top ten performers at the North American box office.
Adriana Caselotti played Snow White in the film.
Snow White is a young princess in the story.
Snow White's wicked stepmother has forced her to work as a scullery maid in the castle.
Despite her circumstances, Snow White retains a cheerful but naïve demeanor.
